key_insight: Adaptive superpixels can reduce large 2D diffraction datasets while preserving high-information features and symmetry, making downstream analysis faster and more interpretable.
engineering_relevance: This preprocessing approach can dramatically cut compute and storage costs for 4D-STEM and synchrotron diffraction workflows, enabling scalable phase mapping and AI-based analysis.
method: Group pixels into variable-area superpixels based on information density.
Compare variance-minimizing clustering strategies: K-means (top-down) vs agglomerative clustering (bottom-up).
Speed up superpixel construction with Gaussian random projection before distance-based clustering.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports superior scaling and interpretability for agglomerative clustering, and over 100-fold acceleration for phase mapping with NMF on a 4D-STEM dataset when superpixels are used.
watch_item: Because the method is distance-based and data-dependent, performance may vary with detector geometry, noise, and how well the superpixeling preserves fine structural signals.
paper_title: Using superpixels for interpretable feature reduction in large 2D diffraction datasets
